findings.summary: The group rule refuses a 4-file reading as 'too large for one producer run', which is an obvious false positive of a size check.
findings.evidence: Group membership alone triggers the refusal, so a one-line change in each of docs, athena.toml, ci.yml and one crate file is refused with a message that says the request is too large. The plan's own test asserts that refusal. The failed jobs had 8 (t67q) and 11 (zaj2) deliverables besides CHANGELOG.md. In HISTORY.txt, the four .github commits (c65e1f0, 3c71fbd, a2fc87e, 0cd0111) show that CI jobs in this repo are often small. Fix: Make the group part a conjunction with a small count: refuse when the reading spans all four groups and has more than about 5 deliverables besides CHANGELOG.md. Both failed shapes are still refused. Change the 4-file case to an accepting case, and add a 4-group case with 6 files as the refusing case. Alternatively, keep the rule but change the message so it says the reading spans separable surfaces, not that it is too large.
findings.location: Plan Decision 1 / Demonstration 3 (refused case 'docs + athena.toml + a workflow + a crate file (groups alone, 4 files)')

findings.summary: docs/decisions.md is a routine record that commonly accompanies code changes, but the plan counts it as a separable surface, the same as a design doc.
findings.evidence: In HISTORY.txt, many single-surface code commits also touch docs/decisions.md (6ae8f66, afcb3da, 620c657, 06e152d, f3dbb29, 49cd05e). Adding a decision entry should not be what pushes a config + ci + code job over the bound. That is the same reason CHANGELOG.md is excluded. Fix: Treat docs/decisions.md like CHANGELOG.md for the group computation, or say in the doc comment why a decisions entry counts as its own surface. Add a unit case either way.
findings.location: Plan Step 1 (job_groups: 'a path under docs/ ... gives Docs')

findings.summary: run/tests.rs calls the real check_reading_text in real_rules(), rules_refusing_the_marker() and a counting closure (around lines 1810–2140), but the Dependents list does not include it.
findings.evidence: A grep for check_reading_text( finds crates/athena-core/src/run/tests.rs:1813, 1820 and 2138. The plan mentions run/tests.rs only in a risk note and through criterion 6. Fix: Add a dependents entry for run/tests.rs. State that its readings stay under 4 groups and 30 deliverables, and that `cargo test --locked` (criterion 6) covers it.

findings.summary: The open question about the count backstop could also offer the conjunction option from the first finding.
findings.evidence: The plan asks only about 30 versus a lower count or a count above 31. Fix: When raising the backstop with the user, also mention the four-groups-plus-minimum-count option.

summary: I read checks.rs (refusing_check at 518–548, CONFIG_FILES at 577, check_scope_limit at 705, normalized_path at 775), the reading.rs test fixtures (scoped_reading with capability "change", governed_reading, gate_refuser, limited, and the scope-limit doc test that looks up the CHANGELOG item with a find on "reading::check_scope_limit"), replay.rs (declared_percent, replay_declaration and replay_declaration_of, the 5-point margin and the 25% reason threshold), the anchor and INPUT_FORMS in refusal_corpus.rs, and HISTORY.txt. Everything the plan names exists where it says. "expected 6% of newly refused readings" parses to Some(6), which matches accepted criterion 5. I checked the claim that "0 of 200 landed commits span all four groups": only four commits touch .github/ (c65e1f0, 3c71fbd, a2fc87e, 0cd0111), and none of them touches athena.toml. 6e7fd3a has 31 paths besides CHANGELOG.md. The new step goes second, and no adjacency test pins that position. Each demonstration names a real production seam (refusing_check through gate_refuser, check_job_size, replay_declaration, include_str source text), uses no double, and would fail without the step line. The readers of refusing_check, check_reading_acceptance and check_reading_text are in steward.rs, run/tests.rs, replay.rs, main.rs, drain.rs and the corpus. The dependents list or the risk notes cover all of them, and criterion 6 runs every one. The approach is defensible: the request names the failure class as multi-surface, the plan sets its bounds from landed history and not from guesses, and it admits its known misses. I have three soundness concerns, all minor: the group rule refuses a tiny reading as "too large"; docs/decisions.md counts as a separate surface even though it is routine; and run/tests.rs is not listed as a dependent. None of them stops any criterion from being shown.
